title: Generation and Recovery of β-cell Spheroids From Step-growth PEG-peptide Hydrogels
protocol: Synthesize 4-arm PEG-norbornene (PEG4NB) using established protocols.
Synthesize photoinitiator Lithium arylphosphanate (LAP) using established protocols.
Calculate the amount of resin needed based on the substitution ratio and synthesis scale.
Swell Rink-amide MBHA resin in dimethylformamide (DMF) for 15 min.

Remove Fmoc-protecting group from the resin using a deprotection solution containing 20% Piperidine and 0.1 M HOBt in DMF at 75 °C for 3 min with power of 20 W for 0.1 mmole scale or 50 W for 0.2 mmole scale.
Rinse the resin with DMF following deprotection.
Perform Ninhydrin test to confirm removal of Fmoc (exposure of N-terminal amine).
Couple the first Fmoc-amino acid at the C-terminus in an activator base solution using parameters of 75 °C for 5 min with power of 20 W for 0.1 mmole scale or 50 W for 0.2 mmole scale.
Synthesize bis-cysteine containing chymotrypsin-sensitive peptide CGGY↓C using standard solid phase peptide synthesis in a microwave peptide synthesizer.
Rinse the resin and perform Ninhydrin test to qualitatively confirm the completion of coupling (disappearance of N-terminal amine).
Drain the resin vessel, rinse resin with dichloromethane to remove DMF.
Prepare cleavage cocktail by mixing 250 mg phenol in 4.75 ml trifluoroacetic acid, 0.125 ml triisopropylsilane and 0.125 ml ddH2O.
Add cleavage solution into the resin vessel and cleave for 30 min at 38 °C with microwave power of 20 W.
Collect peptide solution in a centrifuge tube using vacuum manifold.
Precipitate cleaved peptide in ether, vortex the tube and centrifuge at 3,000 rpm for 5 min to collect the peptide.
Drain supernatant and repeat step twice.
Collect and dry peptide in vacuum.
Purify the peptide using HPLC and characterize it with mass spectrometry.
Prepare 20 wt% PEG4NB solution in PBS.
Vortex the mixture until the macromer dissolves completely.
Sterilize the macromer solution using a syringe filter.
Store the sterilized solution at -20 °C.
Prepare and sterilize 2 wt% photoinitiator (LAP) solution in PBS.
Store the sterilized solution at room temperature protected from light.
Dissolve the peptide (CGGYC) in PBS.
Vortex the mixture.
Syringe filter the solution for sterilization.
Aliquot the peptide solution and store at -20 °C until use.
Prevent freeze-thaw cycles.
Determine thiol (-SH) concentration in the prepared peptide solution using Ellman's reagent.
Follow the manufacturer's protocol.
Calculate the required volume of polymer, peptide crosslinker, photoinitiator, and buffer solutions based on the desired gel formulation.
Prepare gelation molds by cutting the top portion off of sterile 1 ml disposable syringes using a razor blade.
Sterilize the syringe molds by autoclave.
Equilibrate high glucose DMEM to 37 °C.
Equilibrate Hank's balanced salt solution (HBSS, Ca2+, Mg2+ free) to 37 °C.
Equilibrate Trypsin-EDTA to 37 °C.
Remove MIN6 β-cell flasks from the CO2 incubator and place them in the laminar flow hood.
Aspirate cell culture media from the flasks.
Rinse cells with HBSS.
Add 3 ml of 2X (0.1%) Trypsin-EDTA to each flask.
Incubate flasks for 4 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Tap flasks gently on the surface of the hood to detach cells completely.
Confirm cell detachment and dissociation using a microscope.
Add equal volume of cell culture medium to neutralize trypsin.
Mix solution well by gentle pipetting.
Transfer mixture to a conical tube and centrifuge for 5 min at 1,000 rpm.
Aspirate supernatant.
Gently re-suspend cells in 4 - 5 ml of culture media.
Determine cell density using 50% Trypan blue buffer in a hemocytometer.
Mix PEG4NB and CGGYC based on a 1:1 thiol to ene ratio.
Mix LAP, cell solution, and HBSS with the required volumes of PEG4NB and CGGYC in a microcentrifuge tube.
Gently mix the solution using a pipette to obtain a homogeneous mixture.
Add 25 μl of the resulting solution to a syringe mold.
Expose the syringe to UV light (365 nm, 5 mW/cm²) for 2 min.
Plunge gels into a sterile 24-well plate containing cell culture medium after photopolymerization.
Incubate the hydrogels in 37 °C and 5% CO₂.
Wash the cell-laden hydrogels in cell culture medium for 30 min to rinse off loosely attached cells and un-crosslinked macromers.
Transfer the gels into fresh medium.
Refresh cell culture media every 2 to 3 days.
Thaw Live/Dead staining reagents at room temperature.
Add PBS according to the number of samples (n) to be stained: Total volume of PBS = n × 500 μl.
Pipette 0.25 μl of Calcein AM and 2 μl of EthD-1 per 1 ml of PBS to the canonical tube containing PBS.
Vortex the solution to mix the components.
Incubate cell-laden hydrogels in Live/Dead staining solution (0.5 ml/sample) for 1 hr at room temperature on an orbital shaker.
Using a pasteur pipette, remove the dye solution and rinse the sample twice with PBS.
Place the sample on a cover slip or glass slide.
Observe and image cells using a confocal microscope.
Prepare 10% AlamarBlue solution in cell culture medium.
Remove hydrogels from incubator and aspirate media without contacting hydrogel.
Incubate cell-laden hydrogels and an empty well (negative control) with 500 μl of 10% AlamarBlue for 16 hr.
Pipette 200 μl of the AlamarBlue solution into a 96-well plate.
Measure fluorescence using a microplate reader (excitation: 560 nm, emission: 590 nm).
Prepare 1 mg/ml trypsin-free α-chymotrypsin solution in HBBS and sterile filter.
Incubate hydrogels with chymotrypsin solution (500 μl per gel) at room temperature with gentle shaking until complete erosion is achieved.
Place the plate on ice for a few minutes to reduce chymotrypsin activity.
Transfer cell solution into 1 ml tube and centrifuge at 300 rpm, 4°C for 2 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant using a pasture pipette.
Gently resuspend the spheroids in HBSS.
Transfer the recovered spheroid solution to a 24-well plate and place on ice.
Acquire phase contrast images of settled spheroids using a light microscope for size analysis.
Measure recovered spheroid diameters using software such as Nikon Element or ImageJ.
Incubate gels in 500 μl of 2 mM low glucose Kerbs-Ringer buffer (KRB) for 1 hr.
Erode the gel and recover cell spheroids using steps F.1 to F.6.
Aspirate supernatant carefully without making contact with cell spheroids.
Resuspend the spheroids in 500 μl of 2 mM low glucose KRB.
Transfer 100 μl of cell spheroid solution to a 0.6 ml tube and place on ice for intracellular ATP quantification.
Split remaining cell spheroid solution into two microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge each half for 2 min at 300 rpm and 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant almost to the bottom of each tube.
Resuspend first half in 1 ml of 25 mM high glucose KRB.
Resuspend second half in 1 ml of 2 mM low glucose KRB.
Gently pipette and transfer solution containing recovered cell spheroids to a 24-well plate.
Incubate the plate for 1 hr at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Transfer the solution to a microcentrifuge tube after incubation.
Centrifuge for 2 min at 1,000 rpm and 4°C.
Transfer 500 μl of supernatant from the centrifuged tube to another microcentrifuge tube and store at 4°C for insulin ELISA.
Prepare a 10 μM ATP solution and perform serial dilutions for standards.
Add 50 μl of cell spheroid solution to a white 96 well plate.
Add 50 μl of CellTiter Glo reagent to each well containing samples and standards.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Measure luminescence count of the samples and standards using a microplate reader.
Calibrate sample ATP concentrations using a linear regression curve generated by the ATP standards.
Determine total ATP concentration in samples and multiply by the sample dilution factor to get intracellular ATP concentration.
Calculate insulin secretion from recovered spheroids by taking the ratio of amount of insulin secreted in high glucose medium to low glucose medium.
Normalize quantified insulin content of cell spheroids with respective amount of intracellular ATP.
